description: Materialize the full who/when/why history of an approval workflow as a Dagster DataFrame asset. Reads every JSON approval token in a shared `approval_dir` (written by HumanApprovalGate, SlackApprovalGate, TeamsApprovalGate — or any external system dropping tokens in that dir) and emits one row per token with columns: partition_key, approved, approver, reason, feedback, decided_at, token_file, upstream_asset, source. Governance-grade audit surface — point Insights at it, join to run history, export to GRC on a schedule. Independent of which component WROTE the token — audits Human/Slack/Teams/external-webhook tokens uniformly. Complements the approval-gate components (read-only, additive, no coupling).

inputs.description: No upstream — reads directly from filesystem.

outputs.description: One DataFrame asset materializing the token audit; rows sorted by `decided_at` DESC.

asset_name.description: Dagster asset name for the audit DataFrame (e.g. `approval_audit`).
asset_name.label: Asset Name

approval_dir.label: Approval Dir
approval_dir.description: Directory of JSON approval tokens (same dir approval-gate components write into). Accepts local paths (`/tmp/approvals`, `~/approvals`) OR cloud URIs (`s3://bucket/prefix`, `gs://bucket/prefix`, `abfs://container@account.dfs.core.windows.net/prefix`). Cloud URIs require the matching fsspec driver: `pip install s3fs` / `gcsfs` / `adlfs` (whichever you use). Local paths never require fsspec.

token_glob.description: Glob pattern for token files. Default `*.json`.
token_glob.label: Token Glob

freshness_max_lag_minutes.description: Freshness policy: warn if audit is older than N minutes.
freshness_max_lag_minutes.label: Freshness Max Lag Minutes

freshness_cron.description: Cron for the freshness policy (paired with max_lag_minutes).
freshness_cron.label: Freshness Cron

schedule_cron.label: Schedule Cron
schedule_cron.description: If set, emit a Dagster schedule that re-materializes this asset on the given cron.
